components.note: 彐 (hand) — the older character shows arms measuring a span
寸 (cùn) gives a loose sound hint to xún

example.hanzi: 他一直在寻找新的工作。
example.pinyin: Tā yìzhí zài xúnzhǎo xīn de gōngzuò.
example.english: He has been looking for a new job.
example.fact: 寻 is a written verb, mostly seen in 寻找 (to look for), 寻求 (to seek) and 寻常 (ordinary). Notices that begin 寻人启事 ('seeking a person') are missing-person ads, and 寻 was once a unit of length of eight 尺.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — the original sense was 'to burn'
肰 (rán) gives the sound — it matches 然 exactly

example.hanzi: 吃完饭，然后我们去散步。
example.pinyin: Chī wán fàn, ránhòu wǒmen qù sànbù.
example.english: After eating, then we'll go for a walk.
example.fact: 然 originally meant 'to burn' (that sense moved to 燃), and was borrowed for 'so, thus'. It anchors many everyday words: 当然 (of course), 突然 (suddenly), 虽然 (although), 然后 (then) and 自然 (natural).

components.note: 米 (rice) — ground grain gives a fine powder
分 (fēn) gives the sound — only the tone differs

example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan chuān fěnsè de qúnzi.
example.english: She likes to wear pink skirts.
example.fact: 粉 means powder, then 'pink' (粉色,粉红) and rice or starch noodles (米粉). 粉丝 is a famous double meaning: it is both 'vermicelli' and the transliteration of 'fans', so 我是他的粉丝 means 'I'm his fan'.

components.note: 一 (a cover) — something laid over to smother
火 (fire) — the thing being put out

example.pinyin: Fēng yì chuī, làzhú jiù miè le.
example.english: The candle went out as soon as the wind blew.
example.fact: 灭 can describe flames or lights going out (灯灭了) and 'to destroy' in 消灭 and 灭绝 (extinction). 灭火 means to put out a fire, and 灭火器 is a fire extinguisher.

components.note: The pieces of 免 (a cap over 口 and 儿) no longer give a reliable picture; learn it as a unit.

example.pinyin: Xuésheng kěyǐ miǎnfèi cānguān.
example.english: Students can visit for free.
example.fact: 免 is the word behind 免费 (free of charge), 免税 (duty-free) and 难免 (hard to avoid). 免得 and 省得 both mean 'so as not to', as in 带把伞，免得淋雨 ('take an umbrella so you won't get wet').

components.note: 阝 (hill/steps) — coming down a slope
夅 (jiàng) gives the sound — it matches 降 exactly

example.pinyin: Míngtiān qìwēn huì xiàjiàng.
example.english: The temperature will drop tomorrow.
example.fact: 降 has two readings: jiàng is 'to fall or lower' (降价, 降落, 降温) and xiáng is 'to surrender' (投降). The two are written the same, so watch the context.

components.note: This is the simplified form of 獲; its parts are not a dependable clue, so treat it as one unit.

example.hanzi: 他在比赛中获得了第一名。
example.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng huòdé le dì yī míng.
example.english: He won first place in the competition.
example.fact: 获 is formal and mostly in compounds: 获得 (to obtain), 获奖 (win an award), 收获 (harvest or gain) and 获胜 (win). It originally referred to catching game.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — a lofty height
隹 (bird) — a bird set above a mountain

example.hanzi: 崔老师是我们的班主任。
example.pinyin: Cuī lǎoshī shì wǒmen de bānzhǔrèn.
example.english: Teacher Cui is our class teacher.
example.fact: 崔 is a surname. The same character is the Korean surname Choi (최), which makes it a common name in both China and Korea; its literary meaning 'lofty' is no longer used.

excludeSuggestion: Essentially only used as a surname; no everyday word use.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house full of goods
畐 (fú) gives the sound — close to fù

example.hanzi: 他家很富，但是他很朴素。
example.pinyin: Tā jiā hěn fù, dànshì tā hěn púsù.
example.english: His family is wealthy, but he is simple.
example.fact: 富 means rich or abundant. 富有 means 'wealthy' or 'rich in', 财富 is wealth, and 富 is also in the name 富士山 (Mount Fuji) and in 富强 'prosperous and strong'. A rich person is 有钱人 in everyday talk.

components.note: A person standing with both feet planted on the ground line below.

example.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā lìzhèng zhàn hǎo.
example.english: Everyone please stand at attention.
example.fact: 立 is the base for 立刻 (immediately), 成立 (to found), 独立 (independent) and 立场 (standpoint). In the solar calendar 立春 (start of spring) and 立秋 begin the seasons.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement
束 (shù) gives the sound — close to sù

example.pinyin: Qìchē de sùdù hěn kuài.
example.english: The car's speed is very fast.
example.fact: 速 is formal: 速度 (speed), 快速 (rapid), 高速 (high-speed), and 高速公路 is an expressway. In Taiwan, 速食 is 'fast food' where the mainland says 快餐.

components.note: 足 (foot) — the limbs touching the ground
八 (bā) gives the sound — close to pā

example.pinyin: Tā pā zài zhuōzi shàng shuìzháo le.
example.english: He fell asleep lying on the desk.
example.fact: 趴 describes lying face-down or leaning your upper body on something: 趴着睡 is sleeping on one's stomach. In the command 趴下! it means 'get down!'. Taiwan also uses 趴 for 'percent'.

components.note: Traditional accounts tie this shape to subjugation (an eye pierced by a blade), but scholars differ, so treat it as a unit.

example.hanzi: 这个国家的人民很友好。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de rénmín hěn yǒuhǎo.
example.english: The people of this country are very friendly.
example.fact: 民 is bound in compounds like 人民 (the people), 国民 (citizens), 居民 (residents) and 民族 (ethnic group). The proverb 民以食为天 says that 'food is heaven to the people'.

components.note: 羽 (feathers) — feathers sticking up at the end
尧 (yáo) gives a loose sound hint

example.hanzi: 小狗的尾巴翘得高高的。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu de wěiba qiào de gāogāo de.
example.english: The puppy's tail is sticking up high.
example.fact: 翘 has two readings: qiào, 'to curl up, warp' (翘课 means 'to skip class') and qiáo, 'to raise', as in 翘二郎腿 ('cross one's legs') or 翘首 ('to crane one's neck'). 翘楚 means an outstanding person.

components.note: 阝 (hill/slope) — a steep, hazardous place
佥 (qiān) gives a loose sound hint to xiǎn

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo shānlù hěn wēixiǎn.
example.english: This mountain road is very dangerous.
example.fact: 险 builds 危险 (dangerous), 保险 (insurance, literally 'guarantee against danger') and 探险 (to explore). 险些 / 险 as an adverb means 'nearly, narrowly', as in 险些摔倒 'nearly fell'.

components.note: 穴 (cave/hole) — an opening in a building
囱 (cōng) gives the sound — close to chuāng

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ chuānghu dǎkāi.
example.english: Please open the window.
example.fact: 窗 is a window, mostly as 窗户 or 窗口; its measure word is 扇 (一扇窗). 窗口 also means a service counter or an app window. 窗外 means 'outside the window'.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a companion is a person
半 (bàn) gives the sound — it matches 伴 exactly

example.hanzi: 他和老伴常常一起散步。
example.pinyin: Tā hé lǎobàn chángcháng yìqǐ sànbù.
example.english: He often takes walks with his wife.
example.fact: 伴 means a companion: 伙伴 (partner), 同伴 (fellow traveller), 伴侣 (mate) and 老伴, an affectionate term for an elderly spouse. As a verb, 陪伴 is 'to keep company' and 伴奏 'to accompany musically'.

components.note: A picture of interlocking curved roof tiles laid in rows.

example.pinyin: Wūdǐng shàng pū zhe hóngsè de wǎ.
example.english: The roof is covered with red tiles.
example.fact: 瓦 is a roof tile (瓦片), and since it is also the abbreviation for 瓦特 'watt', 一百瓦的灯泡 is a 100-watt bulb. 青砖黑瓦 ('gray brick, black tile') describes the look of traditional southern houses.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a building holds things
谷 (gǔ) gives a loose sound hint to róng

example.hanzi: 这个礼堂可以容纳一千人。
example.pinyin: Zhège lǐtáng kěyǐ róngnà yì qiān rén.
example.english: This auditorium can hold a thousand people.
example.fact: 容 means 'to hold' and 'to permit': 容纳 (accommodate), 容易 (easy), 内容 (content), 宽容 (tolerant). 不容 means 'will not allow', as in 不容置疑 ('beyond question').

components.note: 十 (ten) — the meaning side, a loose sign of abundance
化 (huà) gives the sound — close to huá

example.pinyin: Hěn duō huárén zhù zài Xīnjiāpō.
example.english: Many ethnic Chinese live in Singapore.
example.fact: 华 once meant 'flower', the same word as 花. It then grew into 'splendid' (豪华 luxurious, 繁华 bustling) and 'Chinese': 中华 (China), 华人 (people of Chinese descent), 华语 (Mandarin). As a surname it is read Huà.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — done by hand
末 (mò) gives the sound — close to mǒ

example.hanzi: 她在脸上抹了一点面霜。
example.pinyin: Tā zài liǎn shàng mǒ le yìdiǎn miànshuāng.
example.english: She put a little cream on her face.
example.fact: 抹 is read mǒ for 'to smear' (抹黑 means 'to smear someone's name', literally 'paint black') and mā for 'to wipe', as in 抹布 (a rag). It also counts wisps: 一抹微笑 'a trace of a smile'.

components.note: 木 (tree) — villages are surrounded by trees
寸 (cùn) gives the sound — only the tone differs

example.hanzi: 他出生在一个小村子里。
example.pinyin: Tā chūshēng zài yí gè xiǎo cūnzi lǐ.
example.english: He was born in a small village.
example.fact: 村 is a rural village: 村子 (village), 农村 (the countryside), 村民 (villager). It also appears in 地球村 ('global village'), and in some dialects 村 means 'rustic, boorish'.

components.note: The parts (艹 and 冖 over 吕) suggest connected tents in a camp, but the shape is best treated as a unit.

example.hanzi: 这家商店二十四小时营业。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn èrshísì xiǎoshí yíngyè.
example.english: This shop is open 24 hours.
example.fact: 营 means 'a camp': 军营 (barracks), 露营 (to camp), and 'to operate': 营业 (do business), 经营 (manage), 营销 (marketing). 营养 (nutrition) fits the same idea of 'running' nourishment.

components.note: 田 — in this shape it stands for the head (an old form of 囟)
心 (heart) — thinking with heart and mind

example.pinyin: Wǒ zài sīkǎo zhège wèntí.
example.english: I am thinking about this problem.
example.fact: 思 is the root of 思考 (to think), 思想 (thought), 思念 (to miss someone) and, most often of all, 意思 'meaning': 这是什么意思? is 'what does this mean?'.

components.note: A deer in profile, showing the antlered head, the body and the legs; the modern form keeps the head and horns at the top.

example.pinyin: Sēnlín lǐ yǒu yì zhī xiǎo lù.
example.english: There is a fawn in the forest.
example.fact: 鹿 appears in the idiom 指鹿为马 ('point at a deer and call it a horse'), meaning to deliberately twist the truth. 中原逐鹿 'the deer hunt on the Central Plain' means a contest for power. Its homophone 禄 means official salary.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a wife is a woman
彐 (hand) — one traditional account sees a hand taking a woman as a wife

example.pinyin: Tā hé qīzi zhù zài Shànghǎi.
example.english: He lives in Shanghai with his wife.
example.fact: 妻 usually appears in 妻子 (wife) and 夫妻 (married couple), and is more formal than the colloquial 老婆. In compounds it is bound: you rarely say 妻 alone.

components.note: 八 (spreading) — water flowing apart
口 (opening) — the mouth of a valley

example.pinyin: Shāngǔ lǐ hěn ānjìng.
example.english: The valley is very quiet.
example.fact: 谷 is 'valley' (山谷, 峡谷) and, in the simplified script, also 'grain', because 谷 replaced 穀 (谷物, grain crops). 硅谷 is Silicon Valley and 谷歌 is the transliteration of Google.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — hands casting something away
亠 — an upper part of the shape, linked to the old picture of discarding

example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng fàngqì zhège jīhuì.
example.english: He doesn't want to give up this opportunity.
example.fact: 弃 is formal and mostly in compounds: 放弃 (to give up), 废弃 (abandon), 遗弃 (to desert) and 弃权 (to abstain from voting).

components.note: 冫 (a form of water 氵) — the original sense of water breaching an embankment
夬 (guài) means 'to break open' and also lends a rough sound

example.pinyin: Wǒ juédìng míngtiān qù Běijīng.
example.english: I decided to go to Beijing tomorrow.
example.fact: 决 once meant to break open a dam (决堤), and from the idea of 'cutting a clear path' it came to mean 'decide': 决定, 决心 (determination) and 决赛 (finals). 决 also means 'definitely' in 决不 'absolutely not'.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the meaning side, a trader
介 (jiè) is the sound part of the older 价, which shares this shape

example.hanzi: 这个东西的价格太高了。
example.pinyin: Zhège dōngxi de jiàgé tài gāo le.
example.english: The price of this thing is too high.
example.fact: Simplified 价 replaces 價 and is read jià: 价格 (price), 价钱 (price), 价值 (value), 降价 (cut prices). The older 价 read jiè, with a different meaning, is rare and not what you see today.

components.note: 厂 (shelter) — a roofed building, the old shed form
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — close to tīng

example.pinyin: Kètīng lǐ yǒu yì zhāng dà shāfā.
example.english: There is a big sofa in the living room.
example.fact: 厅 is a hall: 客厅 (living room), 餐厅 (restaurant, dining room) and 大厅 (lobby). It also names provincial government departments like 教育厅.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — a heavy overhang pressing down
㔾 (a kneeling person) — someone crushed beneath it

example.pinyin: Tā zāoyù le hěn duō èyùn.
example.english: He met with a lot of misfortune.
example.fact: 厄 is a bound word for misfortune: 厄运 (bad luck), 困厄 (hardship). It is also used in transliterations like 厄瓜多尔 (Ecuador) and 厄尔尼诺 (El Niño).

excludeSuggestion: Bound literary character, mostly in 厄运 and transliterated place names.

components.note: 艹 (plants) — luxuriant growth
非 (fēi) gives the sound — it matches 菲 exactly

example.pinyin: Tā qùnián qùguo Fēilǜbīn.
example.english: He visited the Philippines last year.
example.fact: 菲 is best known in 菲律宾 (the Philippines), and as a feminine given name character, as in the singer 王菲 (Faye Wong). Read fěi, it means 'meager' (菲薄).

excludeSuggestion: Mostly found in transliterated names and given names (菲律宾); little standalone use.

components.note: 氵 (water) — measuring the depth of water
则 (zé) gives the sound — close to cè

example.hanzi: 医生给我测了一下血压。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi wǒ cè le yíxià xuèyā.
example.english: The doctor measured my blood pressure.
example.fact: 测 comes from gauging water depth and now forms 测量 (measure), 测试 (test), 预测 (predict), 猜测 (guess) and 测验 (quiz). In a lab or hospital, 测 + thing is the standard verb: 测体温, 测血压.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — a pair of bows, an image of young and tender things
冫 (two small strokes) — the soft feathery hairs of something young, in one reading

example.pinyin: Tā de shēntǐ hěn ruò.
example.english: His health is weak.
example.fact: 弱 is the opposite of 强: 软弱 (weak), 弱点 (weakness), 弱者 (the weak). After a fraction it means 'a little less than', as in 三分之一弱 (just under one-third).

components.note: 尸 (body) — the body of an animal
毛 (hair/fur) — the furry tail

example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu yáo zhe wěiba pǎo guòlái.
example.english: The puppy ran over wagging its tail.
example.fact: 尾 is a tail or the end of something: 尾巴 (tail), 结尾 (ending), 年尾 (year-end). It is also a measure word for fish in formal writing: 一尾鱼 'a fish'.

components.note: 手 (hand) — rubbing by hand
麻 (má) gives the sound — close to mó

example.hanzi: 冬天他常常摩擦双手取暖。
example.pinyin: Dōngtiān tā chángcháng mócā shuāngshǒu qǔnuǎn.
example.english: In winter he often rubs his hands to keep warm.
example.fact: 摩 means 'to rub', as in 摩擦 (friction), 按摩 (massage) and 摩托车 (motorcycle, from 'motor'). 摩天大楼 is a skyscraper, a building that 'rubs the sky'.

components.note: 氵 (water) — a liquid
夜 (yè) gives the sound — it matches 液 exactly

example.pinyin: Zhè píng yètǐ yǒu yì gǔ suānwèi.
example.english: This bottle of liquid has a sour smell.
example.fact: 液 is a bound word for liquid: 液体 (liquid), 血液 (blood), 溶液 (solution) and 洗手液 (hand sanitizer). It is more scientific than 水, which is the everyday word.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — done by hand
军 (army) — directing troops; also gives a rough sound

example.pinyin: Tā xiàng wǒmen huīshǒu gàobié.
example.english: He waved goodbye to us.
example.fact: 挥 means to wave or swing: 挥手 (wave a hand), 挥舞 (brandish). It also builds 发挥 (bring into play), 指挥 (to command, conduct) and 挥霍 (to squander money).

components.note: 纟 (thread) — the end of a thread, the original sense
冬 (dōng) gives a rough sound clue to zhōng

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōngyú dào jiā le.
example.english: We've finally arrived home.
example.fact: 终 is the 'end' in 终于 (finally, implying a long wait), 终点 (terminus) and 最终 (ultimate). 终身 means 'lifelong' and 始终 means 'from start to finish'.

components.note: 亻 (person) — human relationships
仑 (lún) gives the sound — it matches 伦 exactly

example.hanzi: 这是一个很有意思的伦理问题。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè hěn yǒu yìsi de lúnlǐ wèntí.
example.english: This is a very interesting ethical question.
example.fact: 伦 is a bound word about human order: 伦理 (ethics), 人伦 (human relationships). It is also used in transliterations like 伦敦 (London), and 无与伦比 means 'peerless'.

components.note: A tongue sticking out of an open mouth; the modern form keeps the mouth at the bottom.

example.pinyin: Tā tǔ le tǔ shétou.
example.english: He stuck out his tongue.
example.fact: 舌 is the tongue, usually 舌头 in speech, and it is a part of 舌尖 (tip of the tongue). The documentary 舌尖上的中国 (A Bite of China) is named for this idea. 口舌 can mean 'quarrelling' too.

components.note: 月 (moon) — moonlight, brightness
良 (liáng) gives a loose sound hint to lǎng

example.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì qínglǎng.
example.english: The weather is clear and bright today.
example.fact: 朗 appears in 晴朗 (clear sky), 开朗 (cheerful, outgoing) and in the loud-reading words 朗读 and 朗诵. 朗朗 describes a clear voice, as in 朗朗上口 'easy to read aloud'.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — to hold something off
亢 (kàng) — gives the sound

example.hanzi: 人民起来抗议这项政策。
example.pinyin: Rénmín qǐlái kàngyì zhè xiàng zhèngcè.
example.english: The people rose up to protest this policy.
example.fact: 抗 is 'to resist': 抗议 (protest), 对抗 (to oppose), 抗体 (antibody), 抗生素 (antibiotic) and 抗战, the 'war of resistance' against Japan. It is also a prefix like 'anti-', as in 抗病毒.

components.note: 尹 (a hand holding a staff) — someone in charge
口 (mouth) — giving orders

example.pinyin: Guójūn xiàlìng xiūjiàn xīn qiáo.
example.english: The king ordered a new bridge to be built.
example.fact: 君 is the ruler, and by extension a refined person: 君子 (a gentleman in the Confucian sense). Today it can also be an affectionate suffix after a name, like the Japanese -kun, such as 小明君.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — a perilla herb, the original sense
办 — in this simplified form it replaces the older sound part and is not a real sound clue

example.hanzi: 苏州是一座美丽的城市。
example.pinyin: Sūzhōu shì yí zuò měilì de chéngshì.
example.english: Suzhou is a beautiful city.
example.fact: 苏 abbreviates 江苏 (Jiangsu) and 苏州 (Suzhou), famous in the saying 上有天堂，下有苏杭 ('Heaven above, Suzhou and Hangzhou below'). It is also a surname (the poet 苏轼) and means 'revive' in 复苏.

components.note: 氵 (water) — where things sink
冗 (rǒng) — 'excess', a heavy burden that pulls down

example.hanzi: 这个箱子太沉了，我搬不动。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāngzi tài chén le, wǒ bān bú dòng.
example.english: This box is too heavy; I can't move it.
example.fact: 沉 means 'to sink' (下沉), and colloquially 'heavy': 这个箱子很沉. It also describes states: 沉默 (silent), 沉重 (heavy, serious) and 沉睡 (deep sleep).

components.note: A top-down picture of farm plots divided by paths and ditches.

example.pinyin: Nóngmín zài tián lǐ zhòng shuǐdào.
example.english: The farmers are growing rice in the fields.
example.fact: 田 is a field: 农田, 水田 (paddy), 田野 (open country). 田径 is 'track and field'. 田 is also a common surname.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — an animal led by a rope
冖 (cover/loop) — the rope or halter

example.hanzi: 他牵着孩子的手过马路。
example.pinyin: Tā qiān zhe háizi de shǒu guò mǎlù.
example.english: He led the child across the road by the hand.
example.fact: 牵 is leading by a rope and, by extension, by the hand: 牵手 (hold hands). It also gives 牵挂 ('to worry about, a heart tugged') and 牵涉 (to involve). 牵牛花 is the morning glory.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — a body part
要 (yào) gives the sound — close to yāo; 要 itself began as a picture of the waist

example.pinyin: Wǒ de yāo yǒudiǎn téng.
example.english: My lower back hurts a bit.
example.fact: 腰 covers both the waist and the lower back, so 腰疼 usually means a back ache. 腰带 is a belt and 腰包 a waist pouch; 腰 can also be the waist of trousers.
